# Copilot Instructions — Seven Minute Workout

A phone-first PWA: TanStack Start (React 19 + SSR) → built by Vite → deployed to Cloudflare Workers. No backend; all user data lives in `localStorage`.

## Commands

Bun is the package manager and script runner (not npm). The dev server runs at `http://localhost:8080`.

```bash
bun install
bun run dev          # vite dev
bun run build        # vite build (production)
bun run build:dev    # vite build --mode development
bun run preview      # serve the built bundle
bun run lint         # eslint .
bun run format       # prettier --write .
```

There is **no test suite** in this repo — do not invent test scripts or add a test runner unless the task explicitly calls for it.

To lint a single file: `bun run lint -- path/to/file.tsx`.

## Architecture (the parts you have to read multiple files to understand)

### TanStack Start + Cloudflare Workers, with a custom server entry

`vite.config.ts` extends `@lovable.dev/vite-tanstack-config`, which already bundles `tanstackStart`, `viteReact`, `tailwindcss`, `tsConfigPaths`, the Cloudflare plugin, the `@/` alias, and dev tooling. **Do not add any of those plugins manually** — duplicating them breaks the build. Add extra config via `defineConfig({ vite: { … } })`.

The TanStack Start server entry is redirected to `src/server.ts` in **two places** that must stay in sync:

- `vite.config.ts` → `tanstackStart.server.entry: "server"` (this is what `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` actually builds from)
- `wrangler.jsonc` → `"main": "src/server.ts"`

`src/server.ts` exists because h3 (the underlying request handler) swallows in-handler throws into a JSON 500 response with body `{"unhandled":true,"message":"HTTPError"}`. A plain `try/catch` around the handler never sees those. The wrapper:

1. Calls the TanStack Start server entry.
2. Inspects the response — if status ≥ 500 and the body matches the h3-swallowed shape, it pulls the real error via `consumeLastCapturedError()` (from `src/lib/error-capture.ts`, which listens on `globalThis` `error` / `unhandledrejection`) and replaces the body with the branded HTML from `src/lib/error-page.ts`.
3. `src/start.ts` adds a parallel `errorMiddleware` for errors thrown without a `statusCode` property.

If you're touching server-side error handling, change all three files together (`server.ts`, `start.ts`, `error-capture.ts`).

### Routes are file-based; `routeTree.gen.ts` is generated

Routes live in `src/routes/` (`__root.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `workout.tsx`, `routine.$id.tsx`, `history.tsx`). `src/routeTree.gen.ts` is autogenerated by the TanStack Router plugin — never edit it by hand and it's excluded from Prettier.

`__root.tsx` owns the `<html>` shell, all `<head>` meta/links, the `QueryClientProvider`, and the 404 / error components. App-wide meta tags (viewport, OG, manifest link, fonts) belong here, not in individual routes.

### SSR serialization boundary — the load-bearing convention

**Do not return non-serializable values from route `loader`s or `beforeLoad`s.** TanStack Start serializes these values via `seroval`, which chokes on React components (specifically the `Symbol(react.forward_ref)` tag on things like Lucide icons), functions, class instances, and DOM nodes. A crash here ships partial HTML and the client hydration fails with `Invariant failed`.

The convention in this repo: **pass IDs across the boundary; look up rich objects (with icons, etc.) in the component.** See `src/routes/routine.$id.tsx` — it uses `beforeLoad` only to validate the param and throw `notFound()`, then re-finds the routine from `ROUTINES` inside the component. Don't reintroduce a loader that returns `Routine` objects.

If you add a new route, prefer no loader at all for static reference data. The full case study is in `documentation/2026-05-12 Lessons from the Routine Deep Link Crash.md` — read it before adding loaders.

### Data model

- All persistent state is in `localStorage` via `src/lib/storage.ts`. Keys are versioned (`seven-min-sessions-v1`, `seven-min-selected-routine-v1`) — bump the suffix if you change the shape.
- All `storage.ts` reads must be SSR-safe: guard with `typeof window === "undefined"` and wrap parses in `try/catch`. Follow the existing pattern.
- Static workout data (`ROUTINES`, `EXERCISES`, `WORK_SECONDS`, `REST_SECONDS`, `READY_SECONDS`, `DEFAULT_ROUTINE_ID`) is in `src/lib/workout.ts`. Exercise `icon` fields are Lucide components — they must stay client-side (see SSR note above).

### Audio

`src/lib/audio.ts` lazy-creates a single `AudioContext` and generates beeps via oscillators (no audio files). `unlockAudio()` must be called from a user gesture (e.g., the "Start workout" link's `onClick`) before any sound will play on iOS Safari — it plays a 1-sample silent buffer to satisfy the autoplay gate. Keep this call on any new "start a workout" entry point.

## Conventions

- **Path alias:** `@/*` → `src/*` (configured in `tsconfig.json` and via `vite-tsconfig-paths`). Use `@/components/...`, `@/lib/...`, `@/hooks/...`.
- **UI components:** shadcn/ui (style: `new-york`, base color: `slate`, icons: Lucide) lives in `src/components/ui/`. Add new shadcn components with the shadcn CLI — config is in `components.json`.
- **Styling:** Tailwind v4 via `@tailwindcss/vite`. Global styles + CSS variables in `src/styles.css`, imported in `__root.tsx` via `import appCss from "../styles.css?url"`.
- **Prettier:** 100-column line width, double quotes, semicolons, trailing commas everywhere. Run `bun run format` before committing.
- **ESLint:** Importing `server-only` (the Next.js package) is a hard error — TanStack Start uses `*.server.ts` filename suffixes or `@tanstack/react-start/server-only` instead.
- **PWA / service worker:** intentionally **not** present. `.lovable/plan.md` documents this trade-off. Don't add a service worker without an explicit decision recorded in `documentation/`.
- **Long-form design notes** belong in `documentation/` (dated, `YYYY-MM-DD Title.md`). The README's "Learning log" section is the index.
